newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSSIES CONSIDER SPECIALIST ONE-DAY CAPTAIN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSSIES CONSIDER SPECIALIST ONE-DAY CAPTAIN.

text.p: Australia's test captain should no longer be guaranteed the job of leading the country's limited overs side, chairman of selectors Trevor Hohns said on Monday.
Hohns, who heads a five-man selection panel, is seeking a change of policy to give him authority to pick a specialist captain, if necessary, for one-day matches.
"We would like the freedom to pick a team for each specific type of game and that includes the captain," Hohns told Reuters in a telephone interview from Brisbane.
"Limited overs cricket and test cricket are now miles apart and some players play one-day cricket better than others," Hohns said.
In line with the established policy, current captain Mark Taylor led Australia in both test matches and limited overs internationals on the recent Ashes tour to England.
Australia retained the Ashes by taking an unbeatable 3-1 lead in the six-test series against England, but lost the earlier limited overs series.

Taylor has struggled for form as an opener for long periods during the tour, prompting calls for his sacking as captain and opener. But the burly left-hander has hinted he will stay on as captain if he receives backing from selectors.
"I can't say I am going to captain the side for two more years. I'll do the job if they want me -- but it's not up to me," Taylor told a Sydney newspaper on Sunday.
Hohns said he would contact Taylor on his return from England after the sixth and final test at The Oval, starting on Thursday.
"Obviously his (Taylor's) future would have to be discussed in terms of where he sees himself going and whether he sees himself going on (as captain)," Hohns said.
Australia will face New Zealand and South Africa in test series at home during the coming southern hemisphere season, starting in early November.
After selecting a squad for the first test against New Zealand, Hohns said his panel will recommend a captain and vice-captain from within its ranks.
But he said the final decision on the captaincy would be made by the ACB.
